title: UNEMPLOYMENT DOWN
full_story:
The rate in Clay County fell two tenths of a percent from June to 4.2% and is 1.5% lower than a year ago.  That translates into a drop in the number of unemployed from 238 in June to 214 in July.  The labor force fell from 5,909 in June to 5,637 in July.

The lowest unemployment rate in the region is in Jasper County at 2.8%, down four tenths of a percent from June.  Effingham’s rate was at 2.9% down a half percent from June.  The highest rate in the region was in Marion and Wayne Counties where the rates were 4.2%.  The lowest rate in the state was in Brown County at 2.5%, and the highest rate in the state was in Edwards County at 7.2%.

Total nonfarm employment in the Centralia-Mt. Vernon labor market decreased by 675 jobs from a year ago.  Private education and health services is down 300 jobs, and government is down 100 jobs.  The biggest losses were in professional-business services down 300 jobs, trade-transportation-utilities down 250 jobs, manufacturing down 225 jobs, leisure-hospitality down 175 jobs and financial activities down 125 jobs.

Statewide, unemployment in July was 4.6%, a half of a percent lower than in June.  The National unemployment rate was 4.4% unchanged from June.

title: BLOOD DRIVE
full_story:
The American Red Cross announced an emergency blood shortage on July 13th.  Despite thousands of individuals stepping forward to help, the situation has escalated into a blood supply CRISIS.  For just the second time in history, the Red Cross has issued a national blood CRISIS.  Blood donations have fallen to a four-year summer low, worsening this summer’s emergency shortage.  A blood supply crisis is the most extreme blood shortage, posing a concerning risk to patient care.  Doctors will be forced to make difficult decisions about who receives blood transfusions and who will need to wait until more blood products become available.

The American Red Cross needs your help now so that hospital patients can continue to receive the transfusions they need.  All blood types are needed, but the situation is especially dire for type O blood as the Red Cross is now limiting distribution of these blood products to hospitals.  The type O positive blood supply has fallen below a one-day supply.  Blood donors are needed immediately to ensure hospitals have the blood they need for patients whose lives depend on transfusions.

To ease the shortage the American Red Cross has scheduled a Blood Drive for this afternoon at the Clay City High School from 1 to 5 pm sponsored by the Clay City High School Student Council.  By donating at this drive, donors are helping one or more graduating seniors earn a scholarship.

After today’s drive there will be a Blood Drive on Friday, September 25th at the Clay County Health Department from 1 to 5 pm.  By donating at this drive, donors will get a $15 e-gift card.

title: ELM RIVER CHOWDER
full_story:
The Elm River Chowder will be held on Saturday, at the Chowder Grounds.  Cost of the chowder is by donation.  Chowder will be for sale by the bowl with seating available and chowder will also be dipped by the bulk at around 12:30 pm.  Please, do not bring glass or plastic containers.

There will also be pulled pork sandwiches, nachos, hot dogs, pie by the slice or whole, and cold drinks.

The Elm River chowder grounds are either six miles south of Clay City off of Route 50 or four miles east of the Rinard Crossroads off of Route 45, watch for signs.

The Elm River Chowder is an over 100 year tradition, funded entirely by donation.  Vegetable prep will begin at 7 am, volunteers are welcome.  For more information, find the Elm River Chowder on Facebook.

title: GRAZING SCHOOLS
full_story:
The Illinois Grazing Lands Coalition (ILGLC) will host two grazing schools in September to give farmers around the state hands-on, practical instruction to help them implement and expand managed grazing on their operations.

The events will be held at the Evan Schuette beef cattle farm in Iuka on September 12th and Greg Thoren’s beef cattle farm in Stockton on September 18th.

Each school combines classroom-style instruction with in-field, pasture-based learning led by the host farmers, ILGLC staff and other experienced graziers.  Topics will focus on soil and pasture health, basics of adaptive grazing, water and fencing systems, multispecies grazing and winter grazing strategies.

Registration is $25 per attendee and is required in advance.  Visit the website ilgrazinglands.org/events to register or for more information.

title: I70 ACCIDENT
full_story:
On Saturday at approximately 10:32 am, the Effingham Fire Department was dispatched to Interstate 70 west, just east of Mile Marker 90, for a reported crash involving two semi-trucks, with one of the vehicles on fire.

Firefighters found two semi-trucks involved in the crash, upon arrival, with one tractor-trailer heavily involved in fire.  Debris and cargo from the crash covered both westbound lanes of Interstate 70.  Firefighters deployed a hose line and used water and firefighting foam to control and extinguish the fire.

Due to the fire, extensive debris, and fluid spills, both westbound lanes were closed, and the Illinois Department of Transportation shut down westbound I-70 at the I-57/I-70 split while emergency crews worked at the scene.  No hazardous cargo was reported.

One driver was transported to St. Anthony’s Memorial Hospital with minor injuries.  The second driver was evaluated at the scene and declined transport.  No other injuries were reported.

The Effingham Fire Department was assisted by the Shumway Fire Protection District, Altamont Fire Department, RuralMed EMS, Illinois State Police, and Illinois Department of Transportation, along with additional personnel and resources involved in the cleanup of the roadway.

The crash and circumstances surrounding the incident are being investigated by the Illinois State Police.

title: SUMMERFIELD COMPLETES HER DOCTORATE
full_story:
The Clemence Elizabeth Cox Scholarship Fund through the Jerry L. Cox Foundation has provided many students pursuing careers in the medical field with the resources needed to achieve their dreams.  The scholarship provides financial assistance to individuals entering the healthcare profession, as well as those pursuing advanced degrees.  Assistance is available for tuition, books, and other direct educational expenses.

The most recent scholarship recipient is Cheyenne Summerfield, who recently completed her Doctor of Physical Therapy degree.

As Fairfield Memorial Hospital continues to expand its healthcare services, including the addition of orthopedic surgeon Dr. Sean Odell and physician assistant John Nugent, while also growing their Skilled Care and Swing Bed services, the need for quality therapy services continues to grow.

Now serving as a Physical Therapist at Fairfield Memorial Hospital, Cheyenne Summerfield is putting her education into practice by providing compassionate, high-quality care to patients throughout the region.  Fairfield Memorial Hospital congratulates Cheyenne on earning her Doctor of Physical Therapy degree and thanks the Jerry L. Cox Foundation for investing in the education and success of healthcare professionals who make a lasting difference in the communities they serve.

Pictured left to right: Nathan Gentz, Foundation Director; Hollie Barrett, MSN, RN, CRHCP, Chief Nursing Officer; Jerry Cox; Cheyenne Summerfield, PT and Mary McCulley, RN BSN CRHCP, Director of Clinical Services
